data.name: SettingsLanguageHint
data.value: Applied at once. Folders and drives WinQEMU creates in a guest from then on are named in this language too (~/Shares, ~/Partages); a guest already set up keeps its names.

data.name: CloneFullCopyHint
data.value: Each disk is copied as it is now into a standalone image. Snapshots are not carried over. The clone depends on nothing afterwards.

data.name: CloneLinkedHint
data.value: Instant and takes almost no space: the clone only stores what it writes and reads the rest from the original's current disks. The original moves onto a new live snapshot named after the clone. While the clone exists, the original can still restore its snapshots, but cannot delete the ones the clone depends on, nor its files. Always move both machines together.

data.name: CloneIdentityHint
data.value: Either way the clone gets its own MAC addresses, but the guest operating system keeps its identity: host name, machine ID, Windows SID. Change them in the clone if it has to share a network with the original.

data.name: CloneFullCopySize
data.value: {0} disk(s), at most {1}, copied into a new folder of the library.

data.name: CloneFullCopySizeUnknown
data.value: {0} disk(s), copied into a new folder of the library.

data.name: CloneLinkedSize
data.value: Nothing is copied: the clone starts with almost empty disks, which only grow by what it writes.

data.name: ConvertWarning
data.value: The conversion writes a new image next to the old one, which is kept, and the machine is attached to the copy. Snapshots are not carried over: they stay on the original image.

data.name: ExportIntro
data.value: An OVA package (OVF 1.0, compressed VMDK disks) that VMware Workstation, ESXi, VirtualBox and Proxmox can import. The machine is exported in its current state.

data.name: ExportSize
data.value: {0} disk(s), at most {1} before compression. During the export, the destination drive needs about twice the package size free.

data.name: ExportFileExists
data.value: This file already exists. Choose another name, or use Browse… to replace it.

data.name: ExportDiskFull
data.value: The destination drive is full. Free up some space or choose another drive.

data.name: GrowHint
data.value: A disk can only grow: shrinking it would cut off the guest's file system, which qemu-img cannot read. The guest only sees the added space once it has extended its partition.

data.name: GrowCurrentSizeUnknown
data.value: Current size unknown: the image has not been measured.

data.name: ImportHint
data.value: The disks are converted to qcow2 in a new folder of the library: the original machine is not changed and remains usable in its hypervisor.

data.name: NewDiskHint
data.value: The image is created in the machine's folder and allocated on demand: on the host it only takes up what the guest writes.

data.name: NewVmTargetFolder
data.value: The machine will be created in:

data.name: NewVmOsHint
data.value: The chosen system presets the firmware, the disk bus, the network card and the clock. Everything can still be changed afterwards.

data.name: NewVmRtcLocal
data.value: Hardware clock in local time (expected by Windows)

data.name: NewVmFormatHint
data.value: qcow2 is sparse: the file only grows as data is written. raw reserves all the space at once.

data.name: NewVmNameExists
data.value: A virtual machine named “{0}” already exists.

data.name: NewVmNoQemu
data.value: QEMU cannot be found: no virtual machine can be created.

data.name: NewVmFolderExists
data.value: The folder {0} already exists. A number will be added to the name so nothing is overwritten.

data.name: NewVmNeedCpu
data.value: At least one virtual processor is needed.

data.name: NewVmNeedMemory
data.value: At least 128 MB of memory is needed.

data.name: NewVmNoUefi
data.value: The requested UEFI firmware is missing from {0}. Choose BIOS or install the edk2 files.

data.name: NewVmSecureBootWhpx
data.value: Secure Boot requires SMM mode, which the WHPX hypervisor does not provide: QEMU would refuse to start. Choose UEFI without Secure Boot.

data.name: NewVmMemoryAdvisory
data.value: The host has {0}. Allocating {1} may push it onto the page file and slow down the whole system.

data.name: NewVmCpuAdvisory
data.value: The host only has {0} logical processors. Beyond that, the vCPUs compete for the same hardware and performance drops.

data.name: NewVmNoWhpx
data.value: WHPX hardware acceleration is unavailable: the VM will run emulated, about ten times slower.

data.name: NewVmNoDiskFile
data.value: Enter the disk file to attach.

data.name: NewVmExistingDiskAdvisory
data.value: The disk is used where it is now, not copied. Moving or deleting it will make the VM unable to start.

data.name: NewVmDiskTooSmall
data.value: The disk must be at least 1 GB.

data.name: NewVmDiskTooLarge
data.value: This wizard limits the disk to 8192 GB.

data.name: NewVmSparseAdvisory
data.value: The disk declares {0} while only {1} is free. The qcow2 format is sparse: it only takes the space actually written, but the guest will run out of space before reaching its stated size.

data.name: NewVmNoSpace
data.value: The {0} format reserves all the space at once, but only {1} is left on the volume.

data.name: NewVmUbuntuPassword
data.value: Ubuntu needs a password to sign in: enter one.

data.name: NewVmNoIsoAdvisory
data.value: Without installation media, the VM will start on an empty disk and stop at the firmware. You can add an ISO later.

data.name: NewVmNoVirtioUnattended
data.value: Without the virtio-win ISO in the second drive, Windows will install without its virtio drivers or the guest agent: no shared folders, and no resolution that follows the window.

data.name: NewVmVirtioSuggested
data.value: For this system, the virtio-win ISO in the second drive lets you use virtio devices (faster network and disk). Optional here, since the disk is set up on a bus recognized natively.

data.name: NewVmUnattendedUbuntu
data.value: Ubuntu installs without asking anything: the whole disk, this account (administrator through sudo), this PC's language, keyboard and time zone, the guest agent and the clipboard agent (shared folders and copy and paste from the start). A NAT card is needed: the packages come from the Internet.

data.name: NewVmUnattendedWindows
data.value: Windows installs without asking anything: the Pro edition, the whole disk, this account (administrator, signed in automatically the first time), this PC's language, keyboard and time zone. Then the virtio drivers and the guest agent, if the virtio-win ISO is in the second drive.

data.name: SettingsQemuHint
data.value: WinQEMU does not install QEMU. Let automatic detection do the work, or point to the folder containing qemu-system-x86_64.exe and qemu-img.exe.

data.name: SettingsQemuOverridden
data.value: Folder set in the settings — automatic detection is turned off.

data.name: SettingsStartAtLogon
data.value: Start WinQEMU when signing in to Windows

data.name: SettingsSoundHint
data.value: The output where all machines play their sound. Windows only remembers it for the QEMU program as a whole: it cannot differ from one machine to another. Volume and mute, however, are set for each machine with the Sound button.

data.name: SettingsLibraryHint
data.value: Folder scanned at startup and offered by default when creating a machine. Changing it rereads the library; no file is moved, and the machines of the previous folder simply disappear from the list.

data.name: SettingsStartAtLogonHint
data.value: WinQEMU then opens in the notification area and starts the machines marked “Start with WinQEMU” (Automatic start section of each machine). Windows also lists it among its startup apps.

data.name: SettingsStartupUnavailable
data.value: Windows does not give access to WinQEMU's startup: {0}

data.name: SettingsStartupDisabledByUser
data.value: Turned off in Windows: turn WinQEMU back on in Settings > Apps > Startup.

data.name: NetworksIntro
data.value: Networks to plug the machines' cards into (Hardware, Network section, “Connection” list). WinQEMU runs them itself; on a private or internal network its DHCP server gives the machines their addresses, on an external network the router does. Each network has its own subnet.

data.name: NetworksTypesHint
data.value: An internal network also connects this PC to the machines, through a TAP-Windows adapter: one adapter per internal network. The driver (from OpenVPN, GPLv2 licence, source github.com/OpenVPN/tap-windows6) comes with WinQEMU and is installed with the first internal network. An external network puts the machines on this PC's network, each with its own address given by the router, thanks to Npcap; there they cannot reach this PC itself (for that: their NAT card, or an internal network).

data.name: NetworksNpcapHint
data.value: An external network goes through Npcap, Wireshark's free capture driver. Install it with its default options, without checking “Restrict Npcap driver's access to Administrators only”, then click “Add an external network” again.

data.name: NetworksInstallingTap
data.value: Installing OpenVPN's TAP-Windows driver… Windows asks for administrator permission, and may ask whether to trust OpenVPN.

data.name: NetworksAddingTap
data.value: Adding a TAP-Windows adapter… Windows asks for administrator permission.

data.name: NetworksNoNewTap
data.value: The driver answered, but no new TAP-Windows adapter appeared. Try again in a moment.

data.name: NetworksTapRefused
data.value: Nothing was installed: administrator permission was refused.

data.name: NetworksNoPhysicalAdapter
data.value: No Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter of this PC is connected: connect one, then try again.

data.name: NetworksInUse
data.value: {0} is used by {1}: first change their network card in Hardware.

data.name: NetworksSaveFailed
data.value: The networks could not be saved: {0}

data.name: GuestFilesHint
data.value: Double-click a folder to open it. Check what to copy: a folder is copied with its contents.

data.name: TrayQuit
data.value: Shut down the machines and quit

data.name: ConsoleIdle
data.value: Start the virtual machine to show its console.

data.name: ConsoleWindowNotFound
data.value: QEMU's console window cannot be found.

data.name: ConsoleEmbedFailed
data.value: The console could not be embedded. It stays in a separate window.

data.name: ConsoleReleaseTimeout
data.value: The console could not be released in time.

data.name: SnapshotsNameTaken
data.value: A snapshot already has this name.

data.name: SnapshotsNoQcow2
data.value: No qcow2 disk: only these disks can hold an internal snapshot.

data.name: SnapshotsNoMemory
data.value: Saving the memory requires migration support, which WHPX lacks: only a machine under TCG emulation allows it. On this machine, a live snapshot only captures the disks, as a power cut would.

data.name: HardwareFileExists
data.value: The file {0} already exists in the machine's folder.

data.name: HardwareMustBeStopped
data.value: The machine must be shut down.

data.name: HardwareNoQemuImg
data.value: qemu-img is not available: QEMU was not detected.

data.name: HardwareDiskFileMissing
data.value: The disk file cannot be found.

data.name: DeployLinkedHint
data.value: Instant and almost free in space: the new machine only records what it writes, and reads the rest from the template's disks, which stay as they are for every machine deployed from it. The template's files cannot be deleted while one of them exists. Always move the template and its machines together.

data.name: SettingsQemuTrademark
data.value: WinQEMU is an independent, unofficial interface for QEMU: it is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by the QEMU project. QEMU is a trademark of Fabrice Bellard.

data.name: ReadinessSubtitle
data.value: What WinQEMU needs to run virtual machines, and what to do about anything missing. Nothing is installed without you.

data.name: ReadinessQemuMissing
data.value: QEMU is not installed, or not where WinQEMU looks for it: no virtual machine can start.

data.name: ReadinessQemuHowTo
data.value: WinQEMU neither bundles nor downloads QEMU. Install it with this command in a terminal, or from its Windows builds' site, then detect it again. If it is installed elsewhere, choose its folder.

data.name: ReadinessWingetName
data.value: Command that installs QEMU with winget

data.name: ReadinessWhpxReady
data.value: Available: machines run at the processor's speed.

data.name: ReadinessWhpxNotEnabled
data.value: The Windows Hypervisor Platform feature is not enabled. WinQEMU can enable it: Windows asks for administrator rights, then a restart.

data.name: ReadinessWhpxRestartOrBlocked
data.value: The feature is enabled but the hypervisor is not running: restart Windows. If it still is not, the hypervisor is kept from starting (bcdedit hypervisorlaunchtype).

data.name: ReadinessWhpxFirmware
data.value: The processor's virtualization is turned off in the PC's firmware: turn it on in the BIOS/UEFI settings (Intel VT-x or AMD-V, often called SVM).

data.name: ReadinessWhpxNotInBuild
data.value: Windows is ready, but this QEMU was built without WHPX: install the Windows build of QEMU.

data.name: ReadinessWhpxRestart
data.value: Windows Hypervisor Platform is enabled: restart Windows for machines to use it.

data.name: ReadinessWhpxDeclined
data.value: Nothing was changed: administrator rights were refused.

data.name: ReadinessWhpxFailed
data.value: The feature could not be enabled ({0}).

data.name: ReadinessTcgNote
data.value: Without acceleration, machines still run, in emulation (TCG), about ten times slower; some guests, Windows 11 among them, become hardly usable.

data.name: NetworksTapHint
data.value: An internal network goes through OpenVPN's free TAP-Windows driver. Install it (Windows asks for administrator permission, and may ask whether to trust OpenVPN), then click “Add an internal network” again.

data.name: CpuFlagsHint
data.value: Ticked features are added to the processor model (+feature). Under WHPX the guest only gets those this PC's processor has. The defaults add what Windows 11 needs.
